source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Council Bluffs OCB1 is a 9 MW regional colocation facility, not a hyperscale AI cluster. At 40 kW per rack, its published IT load supports roughly 225 racks, or under 100 accelerators at four GPUs per rack after non-compute overhead. Its 420,000 square feet of technical space fits a multi-hall regional campus.

The facility's certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, FISMA, TIA-942, and HITRUST, show it is built for regulated enterprise and government workloads. They say nothing about which tenants actually occupy it, so they cannot be read as evidence of AI training demand.

Within Iowa, OCB1 holds half of the state's declared 18 MW and ranks first among the two facilities publishing capacity. Iowa has 52 mapped data center sites, and most publish no power figures at all. Disclosed capacity is the exception, which means state totals understate what is actually built.

What the data does not cover is decisive here. There is no announced expansion, no grid interconnection queue position, no power purchase agreement, and no tenant list. The 9 MW is a published nameplate figure, not a measure of consumption or of constraint on the surrounding grid.
